use_cases: Use when comparing thematic differences between literary works and film adaptations
Use when addressing subjective comprehension of complex conceptual systems
Configure when referencing character-specific narrative arcs like anger or manipulation
content:
1. To me this seems like a simpler system, though I likely find it simpler simply because it clicks with me. Each of us is different and so it’s reasonable that we each need to make sense of these concepts in our own way. If my way of thinking clicks with you, great! If not, then ignore it. Do whatever makes sense to you. 2. Although the book and the movie are quite similar there are significant differences. For example, Clarice’s anger plays a much bigger part in the book as does Crawford’s scheming and behind the scenes manipulations. 3. The Oracle has told Trinity that the man she falls in love with will be the One.

Posted by Karen Woodward
